message.content:
**Famous 19th‑Century Dancers**

| Dancer | Nationality | Notable Contributions |
|--------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1815–1901) | Swedish | Pioneered the “en pointe” technique; star of *La Sylphide* (1832). Her ethereal style defined Romantic ballet. |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1884) | Austrian | Renowned for her virtuosity and dramatic expressiveness; performed across Europe and the United States. |
| **Enrico Cecchetti** (1850–1928) | Italian | Developed the Cecchetti method, a foundational ballet training system still used worldwide. |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Master choreographer of the Imperial Russian Ballet; created classics such as *Swan Lake* (1877) and *The Sleeping Beauty* (1890). |
| **Jean Coralli** (1806–1876) | French | Co‑choreographer of *Giselle* (1841); known for his elegant, narrative ballets. |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1815–1888) | Italian | Influential ballet teacher and theorist; his writings helped codify ballet technique. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1889–1931) | Russian | Though her career peaked in the early 20th century, she was born in the 19th century and became one of the most celebrated ballerinas of all time. |

These dancers were instrumental in shaping ballet’s technical standards, repertoire, and global popularity during the 19th century.
